title: PROJECT FIGHTERS: RAIDS
author: FishBn0es
selftext:
*I've been developing this game with AI for exactly a year. It started as a throwaway project, ended up being something I actually couldn't stop working on. I've been using AI for coding for more than a year now. This type of game is in my mind since I was a child and with the help of AI I'm finnaly able to make it true. Actually... since then, I've gained a lot of coding experience from zero and I can actually bug fix the game, rewrite functions etc.*

A year ago this month I started building a browser game just to mess around. It worked better than expected, people actually played it, so I kept patching it every two weeks. Now it's a fully featured game with working (so-so) online multiplayer.

**PF: RAIDS** is a battle game unlike anything you've seen before .

* 30 playable characters, each with 4 unique abilities and a passive
* 200 NPCs to fight across different game modes
* 14 stories with roguelike elements
* Draft Mode (Normal and Positional): you build a team of 5 and fight a well-trained AI. You really need to know what you're doing to beat it just like in more-advanced stories
* Full item and inventory system: items drop from dailies, stories, quests and challenges
* Crafting: combine items into powerful gear and equip it to your characters
* Character leveling with manual stat allocation
* Quests and a Battle Pass
* Challenges with unique and useful rewards
* Skin system: everything is earnable just by playing
* Working co-op mode: still in beta, and I genuinely need testers

I'm also actively developing a 5v5 PvP mode (you vs. a real player). If things go well, a beta should be out within a month.

  
You can play the game here: [Project Fighters - Login](https://fishb0nes98.github.io/PF-RAID-ONLINE/)  
Check the 1.9 Patch notes: [Patch 1.9 — Project Fighters RAID](https://fishb0nes98.github.io/PF-RAID-ONLINE/patch-1.9.html)

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body: I thought you made a MOBA but its just 5v5 "card" fight. It looks like you make them cards to get around the need to generate animated sprites (or maybe you like the card asethetics) but people expect a certain gameplay experience when they are looking at cards.    Do you actually have players playing the game? I made the same mistake before... adding multiplayer/co-op and then realize nobody plays the game

replies.author: FishBn0es
replies.body:
I don't understand the source of your problems  
Why do I need to use sprites like everyone does for their AI game nowadays...just because you do that, why should I? I like this method, it was the best method last year when AI was less developed. I'll try to make something similar in 3D in the future... but to express my creativity I've found this the best solution... and at least it is not similar to anything people create  
  
What "cards" are you even talking about? Those are not cards... you need to watch 2 mins of the video without fastforwarding to understand how the gameplay flow works... you probably forgot to do that...Since everything have visual, there is "a certain gameplay exprience". And based on feedbacks, it actually works for people, who at least minimally tries to understand the game.

Yes, I have players... but.... even if the game would have 0 player, I don't see the point of not trying to make a working online mode.... I wouldn't consider that a mistake at all. I actually felt like a huge step forwards when I successfully made it happen, and back then I had less than 5 players. It's not like you have 0 player today and tomorrow there will be more than 1000 players playing your game...

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
I was offering my suggestion/feedback as someone who saw your post. As I said in my original comment, I understand why you went for this approach from the technical perspective. (last year sounds right, with sd probably)

I know they are not cards, that's why I put "cards" in quotes in my original comment. I was giving you my honest impression after skimming the video. If you want to improve the promotion effort, I would suggest a better edited video because it is not clear from the initial glance. (I have some idea what you did because many text based ai games also use portraits for their characters)

I apologize if you feel offended but I was just trying to be helpful as a fellow dev. you clearly put in a lot of effort into making this game with the variety of characters. It would be a shame if the trailer video derail that effort. 

on the multiplayer note, I used to feel the same way but what I got from the other devs is that 1) just get a decent playerbase size going first and 2) only spend the effort if there is a need for it. For you project, online play may be a big attraction so I suppose it makes sense for you

good luck with your game
